_note: Gold set for the founding corpus (Evelyn-White, Gutenberg 348). Every question carries the passage that answers it. Answers are entity NAMES resolved against the mesh at evaluation time, never node ids — a gold set pinned to ids would need rebuilding after every read and would encode whatever the retriever returned. Authored from the text, not from memory: the volume has no 'Works and Days', so no Pandora's jar and no golden race; its Pandora is Deucalion's daughter; and the succession passage reads 'Hestia 1618' because footnote markers sit inline. One expected answer was corrected after the fact: 'pomegranate' became 'pomegranate seed', because the corpus reads 'secretly gave her sweet pomegranate seed to eat'. The correction follows the source, not the mesh — adjusting a gold set to match whatever the system happens to hold would make the measurement circular, and the text is what settles it.

_kinds._why: PHX-1066 found that removing co-occurrence edges reads as +2 on the aggregate and is +4 genealogical against -10 narrative. Every claim about this substrate since has been split by question kind for that reason. The split itself was never checked in: it lived as a regex in whatever script measured it that day, and three separate hand-labellings of this set produced 51%, 55% and 57%. A number that cannot be reproduced is not a measurement (PHX-1080).
_kinds._rule: genealogical = at least one expected answer stands in a KINSHIP relation (parent, child, sibling, spouse) to an entity the question names. Everything else is narrative: events, actions, attributes, locations, group membership.

_borderline.fates-names: narrative. Clotho/Lachesis/Atropos ARE children of Night, but the question asks their names as members of a group, not their parentage.
_borderline.aphrodite-birth: narrative. 'From what did Aphrodite grow' is an origin, and the answer is a severed member rather than a parent. The closest call in the set.
_borderline.anchises-aeneas: genealogical. Two-part question; 'whom did she bear him' is kinship, so the whole question counts.
_borderline.hundred-handed: genealogical. Asks for names, but of children named as children of Earth and Heaven.
_borderline.typhoeus-parents: genealogical. 'Youngest child of Earth' is a kinship relation stated as a superlative.
